topic: Electronic Configuration and Position of Elements
title: Your Atom's Address? Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A cinema ticket gives a row and a seat. A letter gives a street and a door. Every element in the periodic table has an address too, and its electrons tell you exactly where it sits. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 3, Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties) Diya notices that sodium and potassium sit in the same column, and we find out why.

On the molecule bench we build sodium electron by electron (2, 8, 1), then chlorine (2, 8, 7) and potassium (2, 8, 8, 1), and read off the address live: the outermost shell gives the period, the subshell of the last electron gives the block, and the valence electrons give the group. A four-step method turns any configuration into period, block and group (s block: outer s electrons, p block: 10 + s + p, d block: s + (n-1)d), and two electrons per orbital explains why period 2 has 8 elements and period 4 has 18. A worked example places Z = 26 (iron) in period 4, group 8, d block. Then the exam trap (chlorine is group 17, not group 7), an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 30 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.
